 Polar Vortex disrupted at the earliest point in a calendar year on record — what happens next?
 Don't run for the hills or dust off the snowplow just yet – this doesn't exactly mean temperatures will drop overnight, or at all.
 By
 Kieran Sullivan , Julian Atienza

 02:32 Polar Vortex disrupted at the earliest point in a calendar year on record 
 The Polar Vortex has been disrupted at the earliest point in a calendar year on record, according to analysis from the FOX Forecast Center. But what does that mean for temperatures later this week and this winter? FOX Weather breaks down all the details.
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 The Polar Vortex has been disrupted at the earliest point in a calendar year on record.
 Any potential cold-weather impacts across North America would likely take several weeks to develop.
 El Niño and a strong Pacific jet stream are expected to favor above-average temperatures across much of the U.S. through December. But what exactly does that mean?
 The Polar Vortex has been disrupted at the earliest point in a calendar year on record, according to analysis from the FOX Forecast Center.   
 Don't run for the hills or dust off the snowplow just yet – this doesn't exactly mean temperatures will drop overnight, or at all.
 POLAR VORTEX: WHAT IS IT? 
 Polar Vortex Tracker. 
 (FOX Weather) 
  What is the polar vortex, and how is it disrupted?
 The polar vortex is a band of strong winds that circles the North Pole from roughly 55 degrees north latitude — approximately the latitude of Ketchikan , Alaska — about 10 to 30 miles above the Earth .
 Seasonal weather patterns in the lower atmosphere can send powerful atmospheric waves into the stratosphere . If those waves are strong enough, they can disrupt the polar vortex by weakening, displacing or splitting the circulation — and, in some cases, reversing its normally strong westerly winds.
 HOW DOES THE POLAR VORTEX INFLUENCE WEATHER? 
 The disruption can alter the circulation of the atmosphere and increase the chances of Arctic air spilling southward.
 Polar Vortex explainer.
 (FOX Weather) 
 In a season of weather extremes dominated by a Super El Niño , this polar vortex disruption could also be one for the books, as it could become the earliest major disruption on record, with potential implications for weather patterns through the rest of fall and eventually into winter .
 Does this mean it's going to be cold? 
 So, will this earliest disruption on record bring loads of snow and train a polar express surge of cold into your town? Not exactly.
 While a polar vortex disruption can lead to colder weather across North America, that does not appear to be the immediate outcome in this case.
 COULD SUPER EL NIÑO PUT A DAMPER ON LAKE-EFFECT SNOW THIS WINTER? 
 Polar Vortex Tracker Forecast. 
 (FOX Weather) 
  "So far, models continue to show no major cold air outbreaks in the future," the FOX Forecast Center said.
 Changes in the stratosphere don't translate into colder weather at the surface overnight. It can take several weeks for those changes to work their way downward and influence the jet stream and larger weather patterns.
 HOW THE BREWING SUPER EL NIÑO WILL BENEFIT VARIOUS REGIONS ACROSS THE COUNTRY 
 Even if this becomes the earliest major breakdown on record, that does not necessarily mean colder air will arrive earlier.
 November CPC temperature impact. 
 (FOX Weather) 
  Any potential impacts across North America would be more likely toward late November or December.
 For now, forecast models continue to show the coldest air pooling across Eastern Europe and Siberia. Meanwhile, North America remains much warmer than average, limiting the chances for a prolonged stretch of Arctic air across the U.S. 
 El Niño impact
 The rapidly strengthening El Niño climate pattern is also expected to play a major role in North American weather through November and into December, with a Super El Niño expected tp be declared later this year.
 THE RIPPLE EFFECT OF EL NIÑO: WHAT DOES IT MEAN AND HOW DOES IT IMPACT THE WORLD'S ECONOMY? 
 El Niño has already begun to strengthen the Pacific jet stream, which is carrying mild air from the Pacific, as well as more storms across the country.
 Influence of El Niño on the Polar Vortex. 
 (FOX Weather) 
  That pattern will support above-average temperatures and make it more difficult for colder air to settle in for an extended period.
 The Climate Prediction Center’s long-range forecasts continue to reflect this pattern, favoring above-average temperatures across much of the northern United States — including the Pacific Northwest , Northern Plains, Upper Midwest , Great Lakes and Northeast — through December.
 HOW TO WATCH FOX WEATHER 
 Brief cool spells remain possible, but the overall pattern currently favors a milder-than-average November and early winter.
